simple: a way of writing GPU programs in C++ that can be built for AMD GPUs and for NVIDIA GPUs from the same source.
analogy: the shared cookbook language both kitchen buildings can read.
precise: AMD's C++ runtime API and kernel language; its host API mirrors the CUDA runtime API with a hip prefix and its kernel language uses CUDA's qualifiers, built-in indices and launch syntax.
source: D1 of F7-01 (AMD, HIP documentation) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); package description read in this build (H1 of F7-01)

simple: AMD's whole software stack for computing on its GPUs: drivers, runtimes, compilers, libraries and tools.
analogy: the second kitchen building itself, with its staff and equipment.
precise: AMD's open software platform for GPU computing, with its own installation guide and per-version compatibility matrix; HIP is its programming interface, the HSA runtime and rocminfo are other parts.
source: D2 of F7-01 (AMD, ROCm documentation) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the command that compiles a HIP program by calling the real compiler for you.
analogy: the prep chef who prepares a card for the stoves of the building it will be cooked in.
precise: HIP's compiler driver: on the AMD platform it runs clang with -x hip and --offload-arch options; on the NVIDIA platform it runs nvcc; HIPCC_VERBOSE=1 prints the command (shown in this build).
source: R1 of F7-06 and R1 of F7-07 (this build's runs); D1 of F7-06 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: which vendor's GPU a HIP build is for: AMD or NVIDIA.
analogy: which building the card is translated for.
precise: the choice between HIP's AMD implementation (ROCm runtime, clang) and its NVIDIA implementation (headers wrapping the CUDA runtime, nvcc); visible as __HIP_PLATFORM_AMD__ or __HIP_PLATFORM_NVIDIA__, which hip_common.h defines from the compiler in use, and selected for hipcc with HIP_PLATFORM.
source: D1 of F7-01 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); H2 of F7-06 (hip_common.h read in this build)

simple: the exact family of AMD GPU the machine code is made for, written like gfx90a.
analogy: the model of stove a card is prepared for.
precise: the processor name passed to --offload-arch and reported by rocminfo as the GPU agent's name; the compiler emits one code object per target, which runs only on GPUs of that target.
source: D5 of F7-01 (LLVM, User Guide for AMDGPU Backend) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R2 of F7-01 (bundle listing in this build)

simple: one executable file that carries the CPU program and the GPU programs together.
analogy: a recipe binder with the head chef's card and one card per stove model.
precise: the container clang writes into a HIP executable: a host entry and one device code object per target, listed by roc-obj-ls (for NVIDIA, the CUDA fat binary listed by cuobjdump).
source: D5 of F7-01 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R2 of F7-01, R3 of F7-02, R8 of F7-07 (this build)

simple: AMD's name for the group of GPU threads that execute together, like NVIDIA's warp.
analogy: a row of helpers, 64 long in the second building's main halls.
precise: the unit of SIMT execution on AMD GPUs; 64 lanes on CDNA targets such as gfx90a and 32 or 64 on RDNA targets; HIP's warpSize holds the compiled target's value (64 for gfx90a, 32 for gfx1030 in this build).
source: D1 and D6 of F7-01 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R2 of F7-07 (compiler output in this build)

simple: AMD's table of which GPUs, Linux versions and kernels a given ROCm release supports.
analogy: the maintenance company's list of stove models it services this year.
precise: a per-version document in the ROCm documentation listing supported GPU architectures and products and operating systems; unlisted hardware is not promised to work, which is not the same as failing.
source: D2 of F7-02 (ROCm documentation) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the part of the operating system that owns an AMD GPU and lets programs use it safely.
analogy: the gas line and the building's maintenance staff.
precise: the Linux amdgpu DRM driver with its compute part (KFD), which provides /dev/kfd and render nodes under /dev/dri used by the ROCm runtime; not a GPU kernel.
source: D2 and D3 of F7-02 (ROCm documentation; Linux kernel GPU driver documentation) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a special file through which a program talks to a driver.
analogy: the locked door of the stove room; you need the right key to go in.
precise: a character or block special file under /dev; the ROCm runtime opens /dev/kfd and a render node, and file permissions decide which users may.
source: D3 of F7-02 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the low-level library that finds the GPUs and hands them work; the HIP runtime sits on top of it.
analogy: the shift supervisor who knows which stoves are lit.
precise: AMD's implementation of the Heterogeneous System Architecture runtime (libhsa-runtime64), which discovers agents through the kernel driver; rocminfo prints what it finds (in this build: 'ROCk module is NOT loaded').
source: D2 of F7-02 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R1 of F7-02 (this build)

simple: a processor the runtime can give work to: a CPU or a GPU.
analogy: a station on the shift supervisor's board.
precise: an HSA term for a device that can execute or dispatch work; each GPU agent's name is its GPU target, such as gfx90a.
source: D2 and D5 of F7-02 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a written list of exactly what software and hardware produced a result.
analogy: the signed clipboard page, with the date.
precise: the OS, kernel release, each ROCm/HIP and CUDA component version as printed by the tools, GPU name and target, and the compatibility-matrix version consulted; required by curriculum E1 and AH-11.
source: R5 of F7-02 (this build); curriculum E1

simple: the functions CPU code calls to use the GPU: get a device, allocate, copy, launch, wait, check errors.
analogy: the names of the stations and tools in a kitchen building.
precise: a C-style host API; CUDA's in cuda_runtime_api.h, HIP's in hip/hip_runtime_api.h, which mirrors CUDA's with the hip prefix and HIP's own hipError_t and hipDeviceProp_t.
source: D1 and D4 of F7-03 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); H1 of F7-03 (headers read in this build)

simple: the list of which HIP name stands for which CUDA name.
analogy: a folded card with old names on the left and new names on the right.
precise: a correspondence between CUDA runtime identifiers and HIP identifiers; documented in the HIP porting guide and HIPIFY tables, and implemented by HIP's NVIDIA back-end header (665 names found there in this build by the course's script).
source: D1 and D2 of F7-03 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R1 of F7-03 (this build)

simple: a tiny function whose whole job is to call another function and translate the answer.
analogy: a sign on the wall that says 'H-pass: this is the C-pass'.
precise: in HIP's NVIDIA back end, an inline static function such as hipFree whose body calls the CUDA function and converts its error code.
source: H2 of F7-03 (nvidia_hip_runtime_api.h read in this build)

simple: turning one runtime's error number into the other's.
analogy: translating the old building's alarm codes into the new building's.
precise: on HIP's NVIDIA back end, hipCUDAErrorTohipError maps cudaError_t to hipError_t and hipErrorToCudaError maps back, for example to ask CUDA for an error's name.
source: H2 of F7-03 (header lines 561 and 971, read in this build)

simple: a C++ mark that makes the compiler warn when a function's result is ignored.
analogy: a ticket that must be signed off, or the manager hears about it.
precise: a C++17 attribute; HIP 5.7 declares hipError_t with it, so every unchecked HIP call warns on both back ends (shown in this build).
source: D5 of F7-03 (C++17 standard) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R6 of F7-03 (this build)

simple: AMD's tools that rewrite CUDA source code into HIP source code.
analogy: translators who rewrite the recipe cards overnight.
precise: a ROCm project with two translators, hipify-perl and hipify-clang, that replace CUDA identifiers and headers with HIP equivalents and report what they could not translate (not installed in this build).
source: D2 of F7-04 (HIPIFY documentation) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the fast HIPIFY translator that swaps names in the text.
analogy: a translator who reads the cards as plain text.
precise: a Perl script applying pattern-based replacements to source text; it does not parse C++ and does not need CUDA headers.
source: D2 of F7-04 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the careful HIPIFY translator that first understands the code as a compiler does.
analogy: a translator who needs the old building's manual on the desk.
precise: a Clang-based tool that parses each CUDA translation unit (so it needs the CUDA headers, include paths and macros of a real compile) and rewrites the identifiers it resolves.
source: D2 and D5 of F7-04 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one source file together with everything it includes, as the compiler sees it.
analogy: one recipe card with all the sub-recipes it refers to clipped to it.
precise: the unit of compilation in C++ after preprocessing; a compiler-based translator works per translation unit with its macros and include paths.
source: D5 of F7-04 (ISO C++, phases of translation) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a built-in function that lets threads of one warp or wavefront exchange values directly.
analogy: passing a bowl along the row of helpers.
precise: device functions such as CUDA's __shfl_down_sync(mask, v, delta) and HIP's __shfl_down(v, delta, width); lane counts and mask widths differ between vendors, so translating them needs a human decision (HIP 5.7 for AMD has no _sync forms in this build).
source: D1 and D4 of F7-04 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R5 of F7-04 (this build)

simple: the GPU's own instructions, written as text, that the compiler produced from a kernel.
analogy: the recipe card as the stove reads it.
precise: the AMDGPU instruction set for a given target (here gfx90a, CDNA2), emitted by clang's AMDGPU back end; kept by hipcc --save-temps.
source: D2 and D5 of F7-05 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R2 of F7-05 (this build)

simple: a register that holds one value for a whole wavefront.
analogy: the number written on the table, the same for every helper at it.
precise: a 32-bit AMD GPU register (s0, s1, …) for values uniform across the wavefront, such as kernel arguments and the block index; counted by the .sgpr_count metadata.
source: D2 of F7-05 (CDNA2 ISA reference) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R2 of F7-05 (this build)

simple: a register that holds a separate value for each lane.
analogy: each helper's own hands.
precise: an AMD GPU register (v0, v1, …) with one 32-bit element per lane of the wavefront, holding per-thread values; counted by .vgpr_count.
source: D2 of F7-05 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R2 of F7-05 (this build)

simple: a row of on/off switches, one per lane, saying which lanes take part in the next vector instruction.
analogy: the helpers in a row who raise their hand for this step.
precise: a 64-bit register on wave64 targets; a per-lane if becomes a compare into vcc and s_and_saveexec_b64, and s_cbranch_execz skips code when no lane is active (gfx1030 used a 32-bit form in this build).
source: D2 of F7-05 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R2 of F7-05 (this build)

simple: the block of memory where a kernel's arguments are placed for it to read.
analogy: the slip clipped to the recipe card with today's quantities.
precise: a memory region whose address the kernel receives in an SGPR pair; arguments sit at fixed offsets (vecAdd: pointers at 0, 8, 16, n at 0x18) and .kernarg_segment_size gives its size (28 bytes here).
source: D5 of F7-05 (LLVM AMDGPU user guide) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R2 of F7-05 (this build)

simple: a command that decides which real compiler and options to use, then runs them.
analogy: the prep chef who decides how to prepare a card for a given stove.
precise: a program such as hipcc, nvcc or clang++ that turns one command line into a sequence of tool invocations.
source: D1 of F7-06 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R1 of F7-06 (this build)

simple: the option that names the GPU model to make machine code for.
analogy: the stove-model box on the plan of work.
precise: a clang option for HIP offloading; each occurrence adds one GPU target and one code object; without it, this build's toolchain chose gfx906 silently.
source: D2 of F7-06 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R2 and R6 of F7-06 (this build)

simple: the CMake setting that lists the AMD GPU models a project is built for.
analogy: the stove-model box on the kitchen's plan of work.
precise: a cache variable defined by the installed hip CMake package (empty by default, initialised from AMDGPU_TARGETS); each entry becomes --offload-arch on hip::device's compile and link flags.
source: H1 of F7-06 (hip-config-amd.cmake read in this build)

simple: a ready-made CMake bundle of the flags and libraries needed to compile GPU code with HIP.
analogy: the prep chef's standard kit, handed to any card that needs a stove.
precise: an imported interface target from find_package(hip); linking to it adds -x hip, the --offload-arch list, --hip-link and the HIP runtime library.
source: D1 of F7-06 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); H1 and R4 of F7-06 (this build)

simple: a name in CMake that stands for something already installed, with its flags attached.
analogy: a labelled box of tools the kitchen bought rather than built.
precise: a CMake target not built by the project that carries usage requirements (include directories, compile options, link libraries) to whatever links to it; defined by a package's config file.
source: D3 of F7-06 (CMake documentation) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the way of building HIP code so that it runs on NVIDIA GPUs, by turning it into CUDA.
analogy: the first building's prep chef cooking a shared-language card on the old stoves.
precise: HIP's NVIDIA platform: hipcc runs nvcc, HIP's headers map every HIP name onto CUDA, and the result is an ordinary CUDA fat binary using the CUDA runtime.
source: D1 of F7-07 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R1 and R8 of F7-07 (this build)

simple: the number of lanes in the warp or wavefront a kernel runs on, readable inside the kernel.
analogy: how long a row of helpers is in the building where the card is cooked.
precise: a device built-in; in HIP 5.7 on AMD a compile-time constant per target (__AMDGCN_WAVEFRONT_SIZE: 64 for gfx90a, 32 for gfx1030), on NVIDIA CUDA's warpSize, read in PTX from WARP_SZ.
source: H1 of F7-07 (headers read in this build); R2 and R4 of F7-07 (this build); D1 of F7-07 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: every lane reads a value from another lane of the same warp or wavefront in one step.
analogy: passing the spoon along the row.
precise: HIP's __shfl_xor(var, lane_mask, width = warpSize) returns var from lane self ^ lane_mask; on AMD built on ds_bpermute, on NVIDIA defined as __shfl_xor_sync(0xffffffff, …) in HIP 5.7.
source: H1 and R5 of F7-07 (this build); D4 and D5 of F7-07 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: adding up a group's values by exchanging with partners at halving distances, so that every lane ends with the total.
analogy: pairs of helpers swapping and adding, then pairs of pairs, until the whole row knows the sum.
precise: a reduction over 2^k lanes with k steps of v += shfl_xor(v, 2^j); it covers exactly the lanes its offsets connect, so its first offset must be half the group size (warpSize / 2).
source: D3 of F7-07 (Harris; CUDA Programming Guide) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R6 of F7-07 (the university's lane model)

simple: an honest label for a result checked only on NVIDIA or only compiled for AMD.
analogy: 'tasted at home only' written on the card.
precise: the university's AH-26 marking, required by the F7 faculty when HIP's NVIDIA back end replaces an AMD GPU for a lab.
source: Guide 5.12 (F7 hardware requirement) and AH-26
